record.paper_title: Graph Partitions: Recent Progresses and Some Open Problems
record.original_question: Let k be an integer at least 2 and let G be a graph with m edges. Define h(m) = sqrt(2m + 1/4) - 1/2. Does V(G) always have a k-partition (V1, V2, ..., Vk) satisfying both of the following bounds: the cross-edge count e(V1, V2, ..., Vk) is at least ((k - 1)/k)m + ((k - 1)/(2k))h(m) - (k - 2)/(8k), and every induced part has at most m/k^2 + ((k - 1)/(2k^2))h(m) edges?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $k\ge 2$ be an integer, and let $G$ be a finite simple graph with $m$ edges and vertex set $V(G)$. Define
$$h(m)=\sqrt{2m+\tfrac14}-\tfrac12.$$
For a partition $(V_1,V_2,\dots,V_k)$ of $V(G)$ into $k$ (possibly empty) parts, let $e(V_i)$ denote the number of edges of $G$ with both endpoints in $V_i$, and let
$$e(V_1,V_2,\dots,V_k)=m-\sum_{i=1}^{k} e(V_i)$$
denote the number of edges of $G$ with endpoints in distinct parts. Does there always exist a partition $(V_1,V_2,\dots,V_k)$ of $V(G)$ such that both of the following hold simultaneously:
$$e(V_1,V_2,\dots,V_k)\ \ge\ \frac{k-1}{k}\,m+\frac{k-1}{2k}\,h(m)-\frac{k-2}{8k},$$
$$\max_{1\le i\le k} e(V_i)\ \le\ \frac{m}{k^2}+\frac{k-1}{2k^2}\,h(m)\,?$$
artifact.status_search_result: Each of the two bounds is known individually (proved by Bollobás and Scott). The question of whether a single partition can achieve both bounds simultaneously was raised by Bollobás and Scott as an open problem (Problem 1 in their judicious-partitions problem list). Recent surveys and work on judicious k-partitions (e.g., Ma and collaborators) discuss progress on related judicious partition problems but the simultaneous version for all k≥2 does not appear to have been fully resolved.
